items.summaryZh: 2026赛季F1阿塞拜疆大奖赛上，凯迪拉克车队两名车手佩雷兹与博塔斯之间的队内差距异常悬殊，排位赛博塔斯慢了1.632秒，正赛中每圈落后约1.9秒。

media.altZh: 博塔斯为何在阿塞拜疆大奖赛上比佩雷兹慢那么多？ · 第 1 张

items.originalTitle: How was Valtteri Bottas so much slower than Sergio Perez in the Azerbaijan GP?
items.summaryEn: In the 2026 Azerbaijan Grand Prix, there was a stark intra-team gap at Cadillac between Sergio Perez and Valtteri Bottas, with Bottas outqualified by 1.632s and losing roughly 1.9s per lap in the race.
detailZh: 博塔斯为何在阿塞拜疆大奖赛上比佩雷兹慢那么多？
巴库的两位凯迪拉克车手之间存在显著的节奏差异——这是他们尽己所知对此的解释
截至目前，在2026赛季F1中，可能还没有哪场比赛的队内表现差距像阿塞拜疆大奖赛上佩雷兹与博塔斯之间的差距如此悬殊。
周五的排位赛中，博塔斯虽受黄旗影响，但仍落后1.632秒，而他的困境一直延续到正赛深处。到第26圈第一次进站时，这位芬兰车手已经落后队友的凯迪拉克超过46秒，相当于每圈损失1.9秒。他比赛后段的节奏也类似，安全车出动之后，他每圈仍被拉开约1.6秒。
“挺漫长的一场比赛，”当被要求描述自己的比赛时，博塔斯紧张地轻笑着说。“说实话，完全没有速度。我只能和费尔南多（阿隆索）斗一斗——当然，我们在那里损失了一些时间。除此之外，差距相当大，所以这个周末有很多东西需要研究。”
这位老将确实不得不采取一些省油滑行的驾驶方式，但他认为这并不能解释他巨大的差距。“我觉得还有别的原因。我们会去查一查，”他说。
与此同时，佩雷斯在第一段比赛中始终跟得上中游车队的节奏。第20圈，当塞恩斯第一次进站时，这位西班牙车手仅领先凯迪拉克一秒；奥迪车队的霍肯伯格和博尔托莱托也没有落后太远。
佩雷斯充分利用了安全车时机，回到赛道时排到了塞恩斯前面，并在重启后的混乱中短暂超越博尔托莱托，一度名列第12位，但最终又跌回到第15位，排在劳森、博尔托莱托和皮亚斯特里身后。
“说实话，这是我在巴库最好的周末之一，我把那辆车的性能发挥到了150%，”这位两届阿塞拜疆大奖赛冠军说道。
“我们一直在和那些因为超车模式而比我们快一到两秒的赛车较量，所以第一段（ stint ）我们始终跟住了他们——和威廉姆斯的车、和奥迪的车，差距很大。但最后在重新发车时，我们就是没有直道速度，所以掉了下去。我们和皮亚斯特里争了一会儿，我想他当时可能有一些损伤。”
“目前我们缺少大约半秒到一秒的速度，才能和他们混在一起竞争。”
“问题其实就是我的速度。我在直道上就像一个活靶子，所以我知道机会不多。”
因此，佩雷兹与博塔斯之间的差距可以用这位墨西哥车手在巴库街道上的进攻性风格来解释：“按照我当时开车的感觉，任何一个弯角只要出一点差错，我都会撞上护墙。所以当你跑完这样一场比赛时，你会感到非常自豪。”
与此同时，博塔斯的比赛在方格旗挥出前不久因技术故障以撞墙告终。
“就在我同一圈，我在1号弯锁死了轮胎，冲出了赛道，”这位凯迪拉克车手解释道。“然后我想是因为多跑了距离，系统有点混乱了。我在15号弯发生了严重打滑，之后当我踩刹车时，只有前刹车起作用，几乎就像后轮不再回收能量了一样。所以，那里有些东西出现了一点混乱。”
这位芬兰车手现在已经连续三场大奖赛，在赛道上没有哪怕一个比赛圈跑在队友前面。
detailEn: How was Valtteri Bottas so much slower than Sergio Perez in the Azerbaijan GP?
There was a significant pace difference between the Cadillac drivers in Baku – here’s how they explain it to the best of their knowledge
There may never have been, so far in the 2026 Formula 1 season, such a stark contrast in intra-team performance as between Sergio Perez and Valtteri Bottas in the Azerbaijan Grand Prix.

Bottas was outqualified by 1.632s on Friday, albeit hindered by a yellow flag, and his woes persisted deep into the race. By his first pitstop on lap 26, the Finn was already over 46 seconds adrift of the sister Cadillac, equating to a 1.9s loss per lap. His late-race pace was similar, as after the safety car interventions he was dropping back by 1.6s a lap.

“Long one,” Bottas nervously chuckled when asked to describe his race. “Honestly, no pace at all. I could only fight with Fernando [Alonso] – for sure, we lost some time there. Otherwise, pretty far off, so lots of things to look into from this weekend.”
The veteran did have to do some lift-and-coast but reckoned that didn’t explain his mammoth deficit. “I think there's something else. We'll have a look,” he said.

Meanwhile, Perez matched the pace of the midfield throughout the first stint. On lap 20, when Carlos Sainz made his first pitstop, the Spaniard led the Cadillac by just one second; Audi pair Nico Hulkenberg and Gabriel Bortoleto weren’t much further down the road.

Perez made the most of the safety car to emerge back on track ahead of Sainz and passed Gabriel Bortoleto to ever so briefly hold 12th following the restart chaos, but eventually fell back down to 15th behind Liam Lawson, Bortoleto and Oscar Piastri.
“It's been one of my best weekends in Baku to be honest, I managed to get 150% out of that car,” the two-time Azerbaijan GP winner said.

“We were fighting cars that are a second or two seconds faster than us due to the overtake mode, so we stayed with them throughout the first stint – with the Williams, with the Audi, big gap. But then in the end at the restart we just don't have any straightline speed, so we fall back. We fought for a bit with Piastri, I think he had some damage.
“At the moment we're lacking really half a second to a second to be able to mix with them.
“The problem is really my pace. I was a sitting duck on the straights, so I knew that there was not much opportunity.”

The gap between Perez and Bottas may therefore be explained by the Mexican’s attacking ethos in the Baku streets: “The way I felt like I was driving, if anything went wrong at any corner I would have put it in the wall. So when you do a race like this, you feel really proud.”
Meanwhile, Bottas’ race ended in the wall due to a technical issue shortly before the checkered flag.

“The same lap I had a lock-up into Turn 1, I went wide,” the Cadillac driver explained. “Then I think the systems got a bit confused because of the extra distance. I had a huge super clip into Turn 15, and then when I hit the brakes, only the front brakes would work, almost like I wasn't harvesting anymore with the rears. So, something got a bit confused there.”
The Finn has now had three consecutive grands prix without spending a single racing lap ahead of his team-mate on the track.

items.summaryZh: 前F1车手胡安·帕布洛·蒙托亚为弗朗哥·科拉平托辩护，尽管后者在阿塞拜疆大奖赛引发了多车相撞事故，他仍欣赏其激进的比赛方式。

items.originalTitle: Juan Pablo Montoya admires Franco Colapinto's "aggressive" approach despite Baku crash
items.summaryEn: Former F1 driver Juan Pablo Montoya has defended Franco Colapinto's aggressive approach despite the Argentine triggering a costly multi-car collision at the Azerbaijan Grand Prix.
detailZh: 胡安·帕布洛·蒙托亚赞赏弗朗哥·科拉平托的激进驾驶风格，尽管发生巴库撞车事故
尽管在阿塞拜疆大奖赛发生代价高昂的多车相撞事故，胡安·帕布洛·蒙托亚仍为弗朗哥·科拉平托的激进驾驶方式辩护
前F1车手胡安·帕布洛·蒙托亚在弗朗哥·科拉平托于阿塞拜疆大奖赛引发代价高昂的多车相撞事故后，仍为其激进驾驶方式辩护。
科拉平托在巴库城市赛道的安全车重启阶段于1号弯引发连环相撞。这位阿根廷车手刹车点判断失误导致车轮锁死，撞上了他的阿尔派队友皮埃尔·加斯利，加斯利随后又撞上了兰多·诺里斯。三名车手全部被迫退赛。
虽然科拉平托在比赛结束后立即道歉，并承认自己“完全失控”，但这起事故还是招致了其他涉事车手的批评。不过，蒙托亚在F1电视的赛后直播节目中谈到了这起撞车，对科拉平托的处理方式提出了不同看法，并给予了称赞。
“我想他预期大家都会刹得很深。问题在于，当你在那么靠后的位置时，就像堵车一样，”这位哥伦比亚车手解释道，“大家不断减速、不断减速。你看他刹车了，眼看就要撞上前面的某个人。”
“所以他选择让开，走到了内侧，而且他几乎把车停住了。他犯了错，撞上了队友，也把兰多撞了出去。他确实犯了一个错误，但情况很惊险。”
弗朗哥·科拉平托，阿尔派；兰多·诺里斯，迈凯伦
他补充道：“这方面难的地方在于你要有攻击性；你看到一个机会，我钦佩敢于尝试的人。当比赛重启时，他们会把它看作一个机会。有些人把重启看作‘我不想丢掉位置’，而弗朗哥是那种想冲上去把握机会的人。
“当你总是像马克斯·维斯塔潘那样，总是看到机会就想去把握的人，你就难免会犯错。”
科拉平托目前在车手积分榜上以27分排名第十二。相比之下，加斯利以41分排名第十。
detailEn: Juan Pablo Montoya admires Franco Colapinto's "aggressive" approach despite Baku crash
Juan Pablo Montoya has defended Franco Colapinto's aggressive approach despite his costly multi-car collision at the Azerbaijan GP
Former Formula 1 driver Juan Pablo Montoya has defended Franco Colapinto's "aggressive" approach following a costly multi-car collision at the Azerbaijan Grand Prix.

Colapinto triggered a Turn 1 pile-up during a safety car restart at the Baku City Circuit. Misjudging his braking point, the Argentinian driver locked up and collided with his Alpine team-mate Pierre Gasly, who in turn crashed into Lando Norris. All three drivers were forced to retire from the grand prix.

While Colapinto apologised immediately after the race and admitted he was "completely out of control", the incident drew criticism from the other drivers involved. But speaking on F1 TV's post-race broadcast, Montoya offered a different view of the crash, praising Colapinto's approach.

"I think he expected everybody to go pretty deep. The problem is when you're so far back it's like a traffic jam," the Colombian explained. "Everybody backs off and backs off. And you see he brakes and he's going to run over somebody.
"So he gets out of the way and gets to the inside, and he nearly stopped the car. He made a mistake and ran over the team-mate and he took Lando out as well. He made a mistake, but it was close."
Franco Colapinto, Alpine, Lando Norris, McLaren

He added: "The hard thing there is you're aggressive; you see an opportunity, and I admire people that try. When you have a restart, they see it as an opportunity. Some people see the restart as, 'I don't want to lose a position,' and Franco is the guy who wants to go and take it.
"When you're always the guy, like Max Verstappen, who always sees an opportunity to take it, you're going to make mistakes."
Colapinto currently sits 12th in the drivers' championship with 27 points. By comparison, Gasly is 10th with 41 points.
keyPointsZh: 事故发生在巴库城市赛道1号弯，当时安全车重启
科拉平托刹车点判断失误锁死车轮，撞上队友加斯利
加斯利随后又撞上诺里斯，三名车手全部退赛
keyPointsEn: The crash occurred at Turn 1 of the Baku City Circuit during a safety car restart
Colapinto misjudged his braking point, locked up and hit his Alpine team-mate Pierre Gasly
Gasly then crashed into Lando Norris, and all three drivers were forced to retire

items.originalTitle: What made Red Bull so fast in the Azerbaijan GP after Max Verstappen’s qualifying issue
items.summaryEn: After fixing Max Verstappen's misbehaving internal combustion engine following qualifying, Red Bull fully exploited its powerful power unit in the Azerbaijan GP, with Verstappen and teammate Isack Hadjar surging to second and third for the team's first double F1 podium.
detailZh: 阿塞拜疆大奖赛红牛缘何在维斯塔潘排位赛问题之后如此之快
红牛在阿塞拜疆大奖赛中充分发挥其强劲动力单元的威力，收获双车领奖台
红牛或许会认为国际汽联对其拥有最强动力单元的评估是一把双刃剑，但在阿塞拜疆大奖赛上，这正是其夺得首个F1双车领奖台的关键。
在排位赛之后修复了维斯塔潘表现异常的内燃机——这一问题导致他在痛苦的第三节排位赛失利、仅列第八位发车之后，他与队友伊萨克·哈贾尔得以在巴库展现红牛的强大实力，分别冲上第二和第三位。
这标志着红牛近两年半以来首次包揽前二名次完赛，车队也承认，如果不是维斯塔潘在排位赛中的困境，他们本来更有可能赢下比赛。
但在本赛季很长一段时间里，这辆车都被认为只是发车区上第四快的赛车，那么这股速度上的转机究竟从何而来？
红牛车队领队洛朗·梅基斯详细说明了几个因素，首先是红牛-福特动力单元：“我们拥有一台出色的动力单元，但它有一个比较窄的最佳使用区间。需要位于米尔顿凯恩斯的团队和赛道边的每一位成员付出大量精力，才能让我们保持在这个狭窄的性能窗口之内。我们每天都在做这件事，这个周末也没有什么不同。”
“每一条赛道都带来了如何做到这一点的挑战，你可以从我们与车手的无线电通话中听到这一点。因此，做好正确的能量管理、正确的动力输出分配以及正确的功率使用，无疑一直是让我们忙个不停的事情。”
众所周知，红牛拥有围场中最强大的内燃机，而将其调校进“相当狭窄的区间”并优化电力输出，意味着它在巴库的直道上拥有充沛的动力。红牛的姐妹车队小红牛使用同款引擎，在正赛的速度陷阱中名列第一，利亚姆·劳森测得349.4公里/小时，而维斯塔潘和哈贾尔也都跻身最高速度前十。
这一利器让两位车手都有能力从前排车手中杀出重围，梅基斯承认，如果不是维斯塔潘在排位赛中遇到引擎故障，本可能取得更好的成绩。
“我们在动力单元上遇到了两个不同的问题，”他说。“这在昨天的排位赛中让我们付出了很大代价。但事实就是这样，这是比赛的一部分。
“平心而论，马克斯从周五开始就非常强势，如果没有动力单元的问题，昨天他本可能争夺头排甚至更好的发车位置。所以当然，今天用新引擎解决了这个问题，让我们恢复了原本期望具备的竞争力。”
维斯塔潘认为巴库是红牛在2026年赢得首胜的最好机会——也可能是最后的机会，因为占据统治地位的车队梅赛德斯将于下周末在（原文如此）马来西亚举行的巴林大奖赛上带来一套重大升级包。
梅基斯呼应了今年一级方程式中升级对性能排序有重大影响这一普遍看法。尽管他的车队承认今年不会再带来另一套重大升级包，他仍然保持乐观，认为车队仍有机会避免自2015年以来首次出现整年无胜绩的一级方程式赛季。
“我们今年已经看到，性能排序会随着升级的时机而交替变化，”他说，“不过我认为重要的是，在从澳大利亚到这里的相当长一段时间里，我们并没有带来大升级包，但我们仍然设法缩小了差距。”
“如果你看看马德里，我们在马德里距离杆位只有百分之一秒半，我想在蒙扎我们距离杆位是百分之二秒。所以我们靠着车队里所有人的努力——底盘方面、动力单元方面、从现有赛车规格中挖掘潜力——缩小了那个差距。然后是的，今天的升级可能又给了我们一点额外优势，把最后那百分之之一秒也吃掉了。
“我们需要看看它在其他赛道上的耐用性如何，然后再决定我们如何应对其他竞争对手。”
detailEn: What made Red Bull so fast in the Azerbaijan GP after Max Verstappen’s qualifying issue
Red Bull fully utilised its punchy power unit in the Azerbaijan GP to great effect to secure a double podium
Red Bull might consider the FIA’s assessment that it has the strongest power unit as a blessing and a curse, but at the Azerbaijan Grand Prix it was key to its first double Formula 1 podium.

After fixing Max Verstappen’s ill-behaving internal combustion engine after qualifying, an issue that triggered his painful Q3 which left him eighth on the grid, both he and team-mate Isack Hadjar were able to demonstrate Red Bull’s prowess in Baku to surge up to second and third respectively.
It marked Red Bull’s first double podium in almost two-and-a-half years and left the team accepting a victory would have been more likely without Verstappen’s qualifying woes.
But where did this turn of pace come from having been considered to have the fourth-fastest car on the grid for long periods of this season?

Red Bull team boss Laurent Mekies detailed a couple of factors, starting with its Red Bull-Ford power unit: “We have a fantastic PU, we have a fairly narrow band to use it at best. And it takes a lot of energy from everyone back in Milton Keynes and on the race track to try to keep us on the narrow window of performance. So that's what we do every day, there was nothing different this weekend.

“Every track comes with this challenge on how you do that and you hear it with our radio communications, with our drivers. So getting the right energy management, getting the right deployment and getting the right power is certainly something that keeps us busy.”

As is well documented, Red Bull has the most powerful internal combustion engine on the grid, and getting it into the “fairly narrow band” along with optimising electrical deployment meant it had plenty of punch on Baku’s straights. Red Bull’s sister squad, Racing Bulls, which runs the same engines, topped the speed trap in the race with Liam Lawson clocking 349.4km/h, while both Verstappen and Hadjar sat into the top 10 for highest speeds.

It was a tool that gave both drivers the ability to carve through the frontrunners and Mekies acknowledged had it not been for Verstappen’s engine problem in qualifying, an even better result was possible.
“We had two different issues in terms of power units,” he said. “It has cost us a lot yesterday [in qualifying]. But that's what it is, that's part of the game.

“I think in fairness Max was very strong from Friday onwards and probably would have been fighting for that first row or more yesterday without the issues we had with the PU. So of course, fixing that today [in the race] with the new engine has allowed us to go back to the competitive level that we were hoping to have.”

Verstappen felt Baku was Red Bull’s best – and potentially last – chance of a first win in 2026 with dominant squad Mercedes set to deliver a major upgrade package next weekend at the Bahrain GP in Malaysia.

Mekies echoed the common theme of upgrades having a major influence on the performance order in F1 this season and, despite his team admitting it will not deliver another major update package this year, he remains optimistic it will still have opportunities to avoid a first win-less F1 season for the team since 2015.

“We have seen this year the pecking order has been alternating based on the timing of the upgrades,” he said. “I think what is however important is that in the fairly long timeframe between Australia and here, where we didn't have a big package coming, we have nonetheless managed to close that gap.

“If you look at Madrid, we were a tenth-and-a-half from pole in Madrid, I think we were two tenths from pole in Monza. So we have managed to close that gap with everyone in the team, chassis side, PU side, extracting from the actual car specifications. And then yes, the upgrades today probably gave us another edge and has eaten up that last tenth.
“We need to see how it's lasting on other tracks and then how we will react to the other competitors.”
